conditions: if big tech fails to make $2 trillion in brand new AI-specific revenue by 2030

statement.excerpt: As a result, based on my analysis, big tech needs to make $2 trillion in brand new revenue, specifically from AI by 2030, or all of this was for nothing.
statement.document_title: NVIDIA Isn't Enron - So What Is It?

from_speaker: big tech needs to make $2 trillion
or all of this was for nothing
our_interpretation: Big tech refers to Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet and Meta, the four companies named immediately before the claim.
Treat the statement as conditional: revenue below the threshold by the deadline implies failure of the AI investment to pay for itself.
Interpret for nothing as failure of economic payback, rather than literally no benefits.
The surrounding discussion of recurring costs suggests annual revenue, but annual versus cumulative revenue is not explicit and remains unresolved.
By 2030 allows through December 31, 2030. Do not substitute an earlier deadline.
Economic payback requires attributable cash benefits, costs and remaining asset value; revenue alone does not measure investment return.
criteria.support_condition: First establish that the specified companies failed the $2 trillion revenue condition by the deadline. Then establish, under a defined investment scope and return measure, that the AI investment failed to pay for itself.
criteria.contradiction_condition: With the below-threshold revenue condition established, demonstrate that the specified AI investment nevertheless paid for itself. Meeting the revenue threshold would leave this conditional untested.
